records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Quotation Handling -->
## Quotation Handling

**Problem:** Strings with unmatched quotes cause parsing errors.

```basic
10 PRINT "HELLO WORLD
```

**Solution:** Always close string literals with matching double quotes.

```basic
10 PRINT "HELLO WORLD"
```

**Escaping quotes:** BASIC v2 has no escape sequence. Use `CHR$(34)` for embedded quotes.

```basic
10 PRINT "HE SAID " + CHR$(34) + "HELLO" + CHR$(34)
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Line Length Limits -->
## Line Length Limits

**Problem:** BASIC lines are limited to 80 characters (2 physical screen lines). Longer lines are truncated or cause errors.

**Solution:** Break long statements across multiple numbered lines.

```basic
10 A=1:B=2:C=3
20 D=A+B+C
```

**Multi-statement lines:** Use `:` to separate statements, but watch total character count.

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Line Numbers -->
## Line Numbers

**Problem:** Line numbers must be 0-63999. Reordering requires renumbering.

**Best practice:** Use increments of 10 (e.g., 10, 20, 30) to leave room for insertions.

```basic
10 REM MAIN LOOP
20 FOR I=1 TO 10
30 PRINT I
40 NEXT I
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Tokenization Issues -->
## Tokenization Issues

**Problem:** BASIC tokenizes keywords in program lines, which affects string matching.

**DATA is not affected:** the tokenizer leaves the rest of a `DATA` statement untokenized, so keywords in `DATA` read back as text.

```basic
10 DATA PRINT,GOTO,END
20 READ A$,B$,C$
30 PRINT A$  :REM DISPLAYS "PRINT"
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Variable Names -->
## Variable Names

**Problem:** Only the first two characters are significant. `SPEED` and `SPECIAL` both resolve to `SP`.

```basic
10 SPEED=10
20 SPECIAL=20
30 PRINT SPEED  :REM PRINTS 20, NOT 10
```

**Solution:** Use unique first-two-character combinations.

```basic
10 SP=10
20 SZ=20
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Array Dimensions -->
## Array Dimensions

**Problem:** Arrays default to dimension 10 (indices 0-10, 11 elements). Using `DIM A(10)` also creates 11 elements (0-10).

**Solution:** Explicitly dimension arrays to the exact size needed and remember the 0 index.

```basic
10 DIM A(9)  :REM CREATES 10 ELEMENTS (0-9)
20 FOR I=0 TO 9
30 A(I)=I*2
40 NEXT I
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#String Concatenation -->
## String Concatenation

**Problem:** String concatenation without spaces can be ambiguous.

```basic
10 A$="HELLO"
20 B$="WORLD"
30 C$=A$+B$  :REM WORKS
40 D$=A$B$   :REM SYNTAX ERROR
```

**Solution:** Always use `+` for concatenation.

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Floating Point Precision -->
## Floating Point Precision

**Problem:** BASIC uses 5-byte floating point with limited precision (~9 digits). Rounding errors accumulate.

```basic
10 A=0.1+0.1+0.1
20 PRINT A=0.3  :REM MAY PRINT 0 (FALSE)
```

**Solution:** Use integer arithmetic when exact values are required, or add small epsilon for comparisons.

```basic
10 A=1+1+1
20 B=A/10
30 IF ABS(B-0.3)<0.0001 THEN PRINT "CLOSE ENOUGH"
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Device Numbers -->
## Device Numbers

**Problem:** Using wrong device numbers causes `FILE NOT FOUND` or hangs.

- Device 0: Keyboard
- Device 1: Cassette
- Device 3: Screen
- Device 4-7: Printers
- Device 8-11: Disk drives

**Solution:** Always verify device numbers before `OPEN` statements.

```basic
10 OPEN 1,8,15,"I0":REM OPEN COMMAND CHANNEL ON DRIVE 8
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Memory Conflicts -->
## Memory Conflicts

**Problem:** The BASIC program, then variables and then arrays grow upward from `$0801`. Strings grow downward from the top of BASIC memory (MEMSIZ; the highest BASIC RAM byte is `$9FFF` by default). They can collide.

**Symptoms:** `OUT OF MEMORY` errors or system crashes.

**Solution:** Monitor free memory with `FRE(0)` and keep programs compact.

```basic
10 PRINT FRE(0)  :REM PRINT FREE BYTES
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#GOTO/GOSUB Loops -->
## GOTO/GOSUB Loops

**Problem:** Excessive `GOSUB` without matching `RETURN` exhausts the stack (limited to ~50 nested calls).

**Solution:** Structure programs with main loops and balanced subroutine calls.

```basic
10 FOR I=1 TO 10
20 GOSUB 100
30 NEXT I
40 END
100 PRINT I
110 RETURN
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Timing and Speed -->
## Timing and Speed

**Problem:** BASIC is interpreted and slow (~1000 statements/sec). Tight loops with many operations lag.

**Solution:** Optimize hot loops, minimize array access, and consider assembly for performance-critical code.

```basic
10 REM SLOW
20 FOR I=1 TO 1000
30 A=A+1:B=B+1:C=C+1
40 NEXT I

10 REM FASTER
20 FOR I=1 TO 1000
30 A=A+1
40 NEXT I:B=A:C=A
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Input Quirks -->
## Input Quirks

**Problem:** `INPUT` statements can be aborted with `STOP` or `RUN/STOP-RESTORE`, leaving variables unchanged or partially set.

**Solution:** Validate inputs and handle empty/invalid responses.

```basic
10 INPUT "ENTER NUMBER";A
20 IF A<1 OR A>100 THEN PRINT "INVALID":GOTO 10
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Screen Codes vs. PETSCII -->
## Screen Codes vs. PETSCII

**Problem:** `PRINT` uses PETSCII codes, but `POKE` to screen memory requires screen codes (different mappings).

**Solution:** Use conversion routines or lookup tables when directly writing to screen RAM ($0400-$07E7).

```basic
10 REM PRINT USES PETSCII
20 PRINT "A"  :REM DISPLAYS 'A'

30 REM POKE TO SCREEN USES SCREEN CODES
40 POKE 1024,1  :REM SCREEN CODE 1 = 'A'
50 POKE 55296,14  :REM SET ITS COLOUR: AFTER A CLEAR, COLOUR RAM HOLDS THE BACKGROUND COLOUR
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#RESTORE Statement -->
## RESTORE Statement

**Problem:** In BASIC V2, `RESTORE` takes no line number. It always resets the `READ` pointer to the start of the program, so the next `READ` uses the first `DATA` statement. To reach later data, `READ` and discard the values before it.

```basic
10 DATA 1,2,3
20 DATA 4,5,6
30 READ A:READ B:READ C
40 RESTORE  :REM BACK TO THE FIRST DATA ITEM
50 FOR I=1 TO 3:READ X:NEXT I  :REM SKIP LINE 10
60 READ D:READ E:READ F  :REM 4,5,6
```

records.name: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-pitfalls.md#Summary -->
## Summary

- **Always close quotes** and watch line lengths (80 chars).
- **Use unique variable prefixes** (first 2 chars matter).
- **Dimension arrays explicitly** and remember 0-indexing.
- **DATA contents are not tokenized**; keywords in DATA read back as text.
- **Check device numbers** before OPEN.
- **Balance GOSUB/RETURN** to avoid stack overflow.
- **Validate INPUT** to handle user errors gracefully.
- **Convert between PETSCII and screen codes** when needed.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#3.1 Variable Types -->
### 3.1 Variable Types

All variables occupy **7 bytes** in the variable table.  
The first two bytes encode the name and type; the remaining bytes store the data or descriptor.

| Type | Suffix | Range | Storage | Notes |
|------|---------|--------|----------|-------|
| **Real (Float)** | none | ±2.94×10⁻³⁹ … ±1.70×10³⁸ | 1-byte exponent + 4-byte mantissa | Default numeric type, ≈9.6-digit precision. |
| **Integer** | `%` | −32768 … 32767 | 2 bytes (hi-lo) | High bit set on both name bytes; slower than float due to conversion. |
| **String** | `$` | 0–255 chars | 1-byte length + 2-byte pointer | High bit set on second name byte; pointer references PETSCII data. |
| **Boolean** | — | `0` (FALSE), `−1` or any non-zero (TRUE) | Numeric representation | Implemented via integers. |

#### Name Encoding

- Only first two letters significant (`CO`, `COCOS` → same variable).  
- Letters A–Z, digits 0–9; must start with a letter.  
- Case-insensitive; stored uppercase.  
- Type suffix distinguishes variants (`A`, `A%`, `A$`).  
- Reserved names: `ST`, `TI`, `TI$`, `FN`, and all keywords.  
- Max name length ≈ 80 characters (logical line length).

**Example collision:**

```
10 A$="1":AA$="2":AAA$="3":PRINT A$,AA$,AAA$
→ 1 3 3
```

---

records.name: data/basic/basic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#3.4 Strings -->
### 3.4 Strings

Strings hold PETSCII text of up to 255 chars.  
The descriptor’s pointer targets either:

- an in-place literal within BASIC text (for quoted constants), or  
- an allocated region in the **string heap** (descending from `FRETOP`).

New strings are created whenever:

- concatenation (`+`),
- substring (`LEFT$`, `MID$`, `RIGHT$`),
- or runtime expression evaluation occurs.

Garbage collection exists (`$B526`): it runs when string space is exhausted and on every `FRE()` call, and can pause the program noticeably. `CLR` or `NEW` frees all strings.

**Efficiency notes**

- Prefer `PRINT A$;B$` instead of `PRINT A$+B$` (no new allocation).  
- Define and reuse variables to prevent heap growth.  
- Direct-mode string operations always allocate temporary strings.

**Advanced manipulation:**  
By modifying the descriptor at `VARTAB` (length and pointer), one can create scrolling or “windowed” text effects without copying data.

---

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#5. Syntax Definition (EBNF) -->
## 5. Syntax Definition (EBNF)

*(Complete grammar retained for program analysis)*

```
program      = { line }, endmarker ;
line         = nextptr word , lineno word , stmtlist , 0x00 ;
stmtlist     = statement , { ":" , statement } ;

statement =
  "REM" , { <any PETSCII except CR> } |
  "FOR" , var , "=" , expr , "TO" , expr , [ "STEP" , expr ] |
  "NEXT" , [ var ] |
  "IF" , expr , "THEN" , ( stmtlist | lineno ) |
  ( "GOTO" | "GO" , "TO" ) , lineno |
  "GOSUB" , lineno | "RETURN" |
  "ON" , expr , ( "GOTO" | "GOSUB" ) , lineno , { "," , lineno } |
  "DEF" , "FN" , fnname , "(" , var , ")" , "=" , expr |
  "INPUT" , [ prompt ] , varlist | "GET" , var | "PRINT" , [ printlist ] |
  "OPEN" , expr , "," , expr , [ "," , expr , [ "," , fnameMode ] ] |
  "CLOSE" , expr | "CMD" , expr , [ "," , exprlist ] |
  "LOAD" , fname [ "," , dev [ "," , secdev ] ] |
  "SAVE" , fname [ "," , dev [ "," , secdev ] ] |
  "VERIFY" , fname [ "," , dev [ "," , secdev ] ] |
  "READ" , varlist | "RESTORE" | "DATA" , datalist |
  "POKE" , expr , "," , expr | "PEEK" , "(" , expr , ")" |
  "WAIT" , expr , "," , expr , [ "," , expr ] |
  "SYS" , expr , { "," , expr } | var , "=" , expr |
  "USR" , "(" , expr , ")" |
  "RUN" , [ lineno ] | "STOP" | "END" | "CONT" |
  "LIST" , [ listRange ] | "NEW" | "CLR" |
  "FRE" , "(" , expr , ")" ;

expr  = term , { "OR" , term } ;
term  = factor , { "AND" , factor } ;
factor= [ "NOT" ] , relation ;
relation = sum , { ( "=" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" | "<>" ) , sum } ;
sum   = product , { ( "+" | "-" ) , product } ;
product = power , { ( "*" | "/" ) , power } ;
power = unary , { "^" , unary } ;
unary = [ "+" | "-" ] , primary ;
primary = number | string | var | fncall | "(" , expr , ")" ;

fncall = ( "SGN" | "INT" | "ABS" | "USR" | "FRE" | "POS" | "SQR" | "RND" |
           "LOG" | "EXP" | "COS" | "SIN" | "TAN" | "ATN" | "PEEK" | "LEN" |
           "STR$" | "VAL" | "ASC" | "CHR$" | "LEFT$" | "RIGHT$" | "MID$" |
           "TAB" | "SPC" ), "(" , [ expr , { "," , expr } ] , ")" ;
```

---

**Flow Control**  
`FOR–TO–STEP–NEXT`, `IF–THEN`, `GOTO`, `GOSUB`, `RETURN`, `ON–GOTO/GOSUB`, `DEF FN`.

**Input/Output**

**File Operations**  
`LOAD`, `SAVE`, `VERIFY`, `OPEN`, `CLOSE`, `CMD`, `ST`.

**Data Access**  
`DATA`, `READ`, `RESTORE`.

**Math / Logic**  
`ABS`, `ATN`, `COS`, `EXP`, `INT`, `LOG`, `RND`, `SGN`, `SIN`, `SQR`, `TAN`;  
Operators `+ − * / ^ AND OR NOT`.

**String Processing**  
`LEN`, `LEFT$`, `RIGHT$`, `MID$`, `STR$`, `VAL`, `ASC`, `CHR$`, `+` (concat).

**Memory / System**  
`PEEK`, `POKE`, `WAIT`, `SYS`, `USR`.

**Program Control**  
`RUN`, `STOP`, `END`, `CONT`, `NEW`, `CLR`, `LIST`, `FRE(0)`.

Constants: `π`, `TI`, `TI$`.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#10.7 Program Structure & I/O -->
### 10.7 Program Structure & I/O

- Put constants/setup early; `DATA` and rarely used routines last.
- Remove `REM` in loops; still parsed.
- Minimise disk/tape/printer I/O; buffer in memory.
- `CMD` redirection is slow—set once.
- Avoid frequent `TI$`; use loop counters instead.
- Use `SYS` for time-critical routines.

records.name: data/basic/basic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#11.2 Screen Handling -->
### 11.2 Screen Handling

- Screen RAM $0400 (1024 dec); Colour RAM $D800 (55296 dec).
- `PRINT` is slow; use direct writes:

  ```basic
  POKE1024+X+40*Y,CHR
  POKE55296+X+40*Y,COLOR
  ```

- Redraw only modified cells; update deltas, not full screen.
- For static backgrounds, draw once, then update moving parts.
- To clear screen, loop over $0400/$D800 ranges.

records.name: data/basic/basic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#11.4 Timing (Delays) -->
### 11.4 Timing (Delays)

- **Do not delay by default**—BASIC is slower than 50 Hz refresh.
- Add timing only for pacing (slow motion, animation rhythm, cross-platform consistency, or sync with music).  
- Implement fixed-step gating, not busy-waits:

  ```basic
  IF TI-T0>=N THEN T0=TI:GOSUB UPDATE
  ```

  → limits maximum update rate without freezing input.
- Avoid `FOR T=1 TO N:NEXT` and tight wait loops; they waste CPU.
- If the game already runs slower than `N`, no wait occurs.

records.name: data/basic/basic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#11.5 Movement & Input -->
### 11.5 Movement & Input

- Move by arithmetic deltas (`X=X+DX`); keep signed `DX/DY`.
- Keyboard: `GET A$` (non-blocking). Avoid `INPUT`.

  ```basic
  GETK$:IFK$<>""THEN...
  ```

- Joystick port 2 @ $DC00 (56320):

  | Bit | Function | Mask |
  |------|-----------|------|
  | 0 | Up | 1 |
  | 1 | Down | 2 |
  | 2 | Left | 4 |
  | 3 | Right | 8 |
  | 4 | Fire | 16 |
  Example:  
  `J=PEEK(56320):IF(JAND1)=0THENPY=PY-1`

records.name: data/basic/basic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/basic/basic-spec.md#11.8 Memory & Performance -->
### 11.8 Memory & Performance

- Use integer arrays for coordinates/counters.  
- Keep < 26 variables for faster lookup.  
- Avoid `PRINT` during play; write HUD directly to screen RAM.  
- For scrolling, shift indices or viewport pointers instead of copying memory.  
- Reuse data structures; avoid new strings inside loop.

records.text:

### 11.9 Example Loop Skeleton

```basic
10 T0=TI:GETK$
20 GOSUB1000:REM LOGIC
30 GOSUB2000:REM DRAW
40 IF TI-T0<2 THEN GOTO40
50 GOTO10
```

→ adds frame pacing only if motion needs slowing.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/context/chat.md -->
# Chat Policy

Behavioral norms for assistants across personas.

## Style

- Be concise, technically precise, and skimmable.
- Use code blocks only for relevant snippets; include provenance comments when injecting source-derived text.
- Use backticks for file, directory, or function names; avoid bare URLs; prefer markdown links with descriptive text.

## Temperature

- Default low temperature; prioritize determinism and repeatability.
- Escalate creativity slightly for SID composition and art prompts.

## Safety & Device Handling

- Warn before potentially disruptive actions (reset, poweroff, drive ops) unless the action is explicitly requested by the user or clearly implied by the requested task (for example, write and run a program).
- Prefer dry runs where possible; confirm preconditions.
- Avoid long-lived processes; commands must terminate.

## Provenance & Transparency

- When injecting templates or retrieved references, add comments like:
  <!-- Source: .github/prompts/compose-song.prompt.md | Section: Compose Song -->
  <!-- Source: data/sound/sid-spec.md -->
- Summarize which layers were used (primer/agent/prompt/policy/RAG) if it helps troubleshooting.

## Formatting

- Use headings and bullet lists; keep responses short by default.
- Embed short code; avoid over-formatting.

## Refusal Policy

- Refuse unsafe or destructive requests; suggest safe alternatives.

### C. MODERN game with REU streaming
| Area | Placement |
|---|---|
| Resident code, IRQ chain, REU/overlay manager, hot tables | main RAM `$0801-$BFFF` (keep small) |
| VIC data (screen, charset, sprites) | VIC bank 3 as in A, refilled from REU between frames |
| Overlay window | fixed RAM window (for example `$D000-$DFFF`) filled by REU fetch; overlay never calls overlay |
| Levels, maps, tilesets, sprite sets, text, SID register streams, samples | REU, one frozen layout file with every offset |
| Config checks at start | UCI present, REU enabled and size sufficient (`c64://ultimate/reu`); show a message and halt otherwise |
- One header file/module (`reu_layout`) defines all REU offsets and sizes. First block carries magic, version, per-block CRC; check at boot, abort loudly on mismatch (stale or empty REU looks like valid data).
- Keep each DMA inside one 512 KB-aligned REU block: VICE increments only the low 19 address bits during a transfer and wraps to the block start (`src/c64/cart/reu.c:1085-1093`). A length register of 0 transfers 65,536 bytes (`reu.c:1534`); guard against it. One 256-byte fetch costs 256 PHI2 cycles at 1 MHz.
- An IRQ that touches REU registers must save and restore them if the main loop also uses REU. Register map, loading paths (UCI load, stash stub) and pitfalls: `c64://ultimate/reu`.
- The host can write at most the 64 KB C64 address space with one `machine:writemem` (measured); larger data reaches the REU through a UCI file load in the game or the REU preload. The preload runs once per firmware start, not on a C64 reset (`1541ultimate@700c7f2fa:software/io/c64/reu_preloader.cc:58-77`).

## Dev loop with c64bridge
1. Choose backend: `c64_select_backend` (`vice` for fast logic/debug, `c64u` for turbo, UCI, Upic, real timing, REU preload).
2. Small code: `c64_program` `upload_run_asm` (built-in assembler: ca65, 64tass, ACME and Kick Assembler spellings of data, fill, align, `.if`, `.include`, `.incbin`, macro and repeat directives; no segments; `data/assembly/assembly-spec.md`). Larger projects: build a PRG with an external assembler (see toolchain), then `c64_program` `run_prg` (`location: "host"` uploads a PRG from the host; `location: "device"` runs one on device storage; VICE takes host paths) or `run_crt`.
3. Verify: `c64_memory` `read_screen`, `wait_for_text`, `read`; `c64_graphics` `capture_frame` (`format: "png"`) for screenshots; `c64_input` `joystick`/`key` to drive the game.
4. Debug (VICE only): `c64_debug` `create_checkpoint` (breakpoint), `wait_for_state`, `get_registers`, `step`. Read `c64://vice/binary-monitor-spec` first.
5. Hardware-only checks: turbo, UCI, Upic, SID layout, REU timing (VICE REU DMA timing differs from the Ultimate), real raster stability. Do not accept VICE timing for modern targets.
6. Capture a frame after every hardware run.

### What modern Ultimate games do differently
- World in REU, fetched on demand (Doom C64U, ReadyOS); load by UCI or preload, not by disk.
- Turbo is detected and measured against the raster counter; the code accepts a 48 MHz maximum (Ultimate 64 MK1) and waits out the forced 1 MHz window after the `run_prg` reset (2.55-2.57 s measured, `c64://gamedev/techniques` section 10).
- Turbo headroom buys software rendering and rich music engines (Doom, Heartbeat), not hardware tricks.
- Upic (border colour changed per pixel) is used for still pictures (Order: Omega, mandelbrot-upic); it needs turbo registers and the UCI palette commands `04 53`/`04 54` (measured on Ultimate 64 Elite 3.15a). Requirements and limits: `c64://ultimate/upic`.
- PCM from REU through Ultimate Audio next to several SIDs.
- UCI for files and TCP, run as a state machine with one step per frame (`c64://ultimate/uci`).
- The program ships a sidecar `.cfg` that sets turbo and REU (rules: `c64://gamedev/toolchain` section 7), and a normal C64 edition runs where those settings are missing (Order: Omega).
- Timing verified on hardware (frame hash, positive controls, tests at 1/16/64 MHz); VICE only for function.

# C64 Game Techniques: IRQ, Sprites, Scrolling, Input, Sound

**Summary:** Compact recipes for the techniques almost every C64 game needs, with fresh minimal 6502 snippets. Snippets use 64tass/KickAssembler-compatible syntax (`* = addr`, `.byte`, `<label`, `>label`, `;` comments); the bridge's built-in assembler (`upload_run_asm`) accepts the basic subset. Anonymous `+` branch labels are 64tass style; rename for other assemblers. The IRQ setup, joystick edge, NTSC skip, LFSR, PAL detect and speed probe snippets were assembled with 64tass and run in VICE 3.10 x64sc; the multiplexer was assembled and its cycles counted from the c64ref cycle table; the open-border steps are Bauer's (Bauer 3.14.1).
**Read when:** implementing display timing, sprites, scrolling, collision, input, music/SFX (also several SIDs), random numbers, PAL/NTSC handling, Ultimate start-up checks (section 10) bitmap and multicolour modes (section 11) or multiply and divide (section 12). Frame structure and budgets: `c64://gamedev/architecture`. Register detail: `c64://graphics/vic/spec`, `c64://io/cia/spec`, `c64://sound/sid/spec`.

Sections 1-3, 6 and 9 end with **Seen in** (open-source projects to study; URLs and licences in `c64://gamedev/references`). Sources: Bauer's VIC-II article (Bauer), Mapping the Commodore 64 and the c64ref ROM disassembly and 6502 tables (mist64/c64ref), the PSID file format (`SID_file_format.txt`), firmware `1541ultimate@700c7f2fa`.

## 9. Compression
- Exomizer 3: `sfx sys` packs a whole PRG, `mem` packs raw streams with the in-game `exodecrunch` routine. Other packers: Pucrunch, ByteBoozer, Doynax LZ, TSCrunch, Subsizer; compare them by measuring decrunch time and size on your own data. RLE and tile dictionaries decode in a single pass over the output.
- Compress level maps, title bitmap, music, text; never per-frame data or hot-path code. Show a screen while a large file decrunches, or unpack the next level while the current one plays.
- MODERN: REU preload or UCI loads avoid decrunch time; compress only for disk or cartridge release. Commands: `c64://gamedev/toolchain`.
**Seen in:** Tony (Exomizer `mem` parts plus `sfx sys`), SquareDoom (disk loader and packed parts).

## 10. MODERN start-up checks (Ultimate only)
Run on the text screen before any raster trick; on failure print a message naming the setting to change and fall back (1 MHz path or refuse). Never decide from the product name. Register details: `c64://ultimate/hardware`.
1. Turbo registers: `lda $d031 / cmp #$ff / beq no_turbo`. After a reset and before any write, `$D031` reads `$00` when `Turbo Control` is `U64 Turbo Registers` or `TurboEnable Bit`, also with Badline Timing Disabled; `$D030` reads `$FF` in `U64 Turbo Registers` and `$FE` in `TurboEnable Bit`; `$D031` reads `$FF` in `Off` and `Manual` (measured on Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20). `$FF` also comes from a stock C64 or VICE, where `$D031` is an unused VIC-II address (Bauer 3.2). Then `lda #$0f / sta $d031` selects speed index 15: 48 MHz on Ultimate 64 / Elite (MK1), 64 MHz on Elite II (`u64/u64_config.cc:324-325`); `$8f` also suppresses bad line and sprite stalls (measured).
2. After the reset that `run_prg` performs, a `$D031` write took effect only 2.55 s (Ultimate 64 Elite 3.15a) and 2.57 s (C64 Ultimate 1.2.1) after program start (`data/ultimate/bench/results/summary.md`). Rewrite `$D031` and run the probe every 0.2 s, at most 15 times (3 s), until two probes in a row agree on a fast result; if it never gets fast, run at 1 MHz.

## 2. Project layout
```
game/
  Makefile
  src/main.asm  src/irq.asm  src/sprites.asm  src/scroll.asm  src/music.asm  src/states/*.asm
  src/memmap.inc          ; every address, size and ROM/RAM choice; build asserts on overlaps
  assets/  charset.ctm  sprites.spd  tune.sid  level*.tmx
  tools/   convert.py     ; asset -> .bin/.asm at build time
  build/   game.prg game.d64 game.crt game.sym game.map
```
- Print a memory report at build time (`-showmem` in Kick, link map elsewhere); fail on overlap.
- Write a label file and pass it as `symbolsFile` to `c64_program` `run_prg`/`load_prg`; `c64_memory` (`read`, `write`, `disassemble`) and `c64_debug` (`create_checkpoint`, `wait_for_state`) then accept label names as addresses. Accepted formats: VICE `al C:0810 .name`, `name = $0810` (64tass, ACME; bare digits are decimal), KickAssembler `.label name=$0810`.
- Label file per tool (each output format checked against `src/tools/translation/symbolRegistry.ts`): cc65 `cl65 -Ln build/game.sym` (VICE format); 64tass 1.60 `-l build/game.sym` (lines `start\t\t= $0810`); KickAssembler 5.25 `-symbolfile` (writes `<source>.sym`, lines `.label start=$810`); ACME `--vicelabels build/game.sym` (lines `al C:0810 .start`, ACME `src/symbol.c`; its `-l` list adds `+2`/`+3` suffixes and `!addr` prefixes that the parser skips); Oscar64 writes `<name>.lbl` (`al 0801 .startup`); llvm-mos writes no label file: convert the ELF with `llvm-nm game.elf | awk '{print $3 " = $" substr($1,5)}'`.

## 3. Makefile skeleton (64tass + Exomizer + c1541; tabs required)
```
AS   = 64tass
FLAGS = -Wall --cbm-prg -l build/game.sym -L build/game.lst
build/game.prg: src/*.asm src/memmap.inc | build
	$(AS) $(FLAGS) -o $@ src/main.asm
build/game.x.prg: build/game.prg
	exomizer sfx sys -o $@ $<
build/game.d64: build/game.x.prg
	c1541 -format "game,01" d64 $@ -write $< game
build:
	mkdir -p build
run: build/game.prg
	x64sc -autostart build/game.prg
```
- Kick: `java -jar KickAss.jar src/main.asm -o build/game.prg -symbolfile`. ACME: `acme -f cbm -o build/game.prg src/main.asm`. cc65: `cl65 -t c64 -o build/game.prg src/main.c`. llvm-mos: `mos-c64-clang -Os -o build/game.prg src/main.c`. Oscar64: `oscar64 -O2 -o=build/game.prg src/main.c` (`-d64=build/game.d64` adds a disk image).
- Exomizer (`exo20info.txt`, `exo31info.txt`): `sfx sys` makes a self-decrunching PRG that jumps to the address of the `SYS` line it finds at the BASIC start; `mem -l none part.bin@0xADDR -o part.exo` writes plain crunched data (no load address) for the in-game decruncher `exodecrs/exodecrunch.s` (decrunches backwards by default).
- BASIC start stub at `$0801`: `10 SYS 2064` bytes `0B 08 0A 00 9E 32 30 36 34 00 00 00`; code starts at `$0810`. Kick: `BasicUpstart2(start)`.

## 4. Formats and packaging
| Output | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.prg` | assembler output | 2-byte load address first; runs on all targets |
| `.d64` | `c1541` (VICE) or `cc1541 -f game -w game.prg game.d64` (cc1541 README; MIT; also sets sector interleave with `-s`) | one file for a single-part game; multipart needs a loader |
| `.crt` | `cartconv -t <type> -i game.bin -o game.crt` (VICE 3.10; `cartconv --types` lists the types, for example Magic Desk and EasyFlash) | MODERN: cartridges that use `$DF00-$DFFF` collide with the REU registers at `$DF00` (`c64://ultimate/reu`) |
| `.sid` | tracker export | input for the player, not an output |
- Loaders: KERNAL `LOAD` (`$FFD5`) needs the KERNAL ROM and I/O banked in (`$01` = `$36` or `$37`); a fastloader (for example Krill's) replaces it for real or emulated drives, per its own documentation. On Ultimate devices, UCI file reads and REU loads bypass the serial bus (`c64://ultimate/uci`, `c64://ultimate/reu`). Disk handling from the bridge: `c64_disk`, `c64_drive`.
- Release set: `.prg` + `.d64` (+ `.crt`), `.cfg` and `.reu` for MODERN (section 7), checksums, README naming target and Ultimate settings.

## 6. Test loop with c64bridge
1. Build on the host, then VICE: `c64_select_backend` `vice`, `run_prg` the PRG with `symbolsFile` (the same call works on Ultimate with `location: "host"`, see step 4). Use `x64sc` (the cycle-based C64 emulator), `-warp` for long loads, and test both video standards with `-pal` and `-ntsc` (VICE 3.10 `doc/vice.texi`).
2. Assert state: `c64_memory` `read`/`wait_for_text`/`read_screen`; `c64_graphics` `capture_frame` PNG; `c64_input` `joystick`.
3. Debug: `c64_debug` `create_checkpoint` on a label name (`address: "game_loop"`), `wait_for_state` for PC, `get_registers`, `step`. Remove checkpoints before timing runs.
4. Hardware gate (MODERN or authentic release): `c64_select_backend` `c64u`, `run_prg` with `location: "host"` and `symbolsFile` (the host PRG is uploaded, 2 to 65,538 bytes; no device storage needed; `location: "device"` runs a PRG already on device storage such as `/Usb0/`); compare a captured frame with VICE; check raster effects, turbo, SID layout, REU/UCI.
5. VICE gaps for MODERN: no UCI, no turbo (`$D030`/`$D031` are unused VIC-II addresses and read `$FF`, Bauer 3.2), no Ultimate Audio. VICE REU DMA moves one byte per CPU cycle plus VIC stalls (`src/c64/cart/reu.c:819-849`); Ultimate rates at turbo speeds are in `c64://ultimate/reu`. VICE loads an REU image (`-reuimage`) only when the file size equals `-reusize` exactly; otherwise it logs "Reading REU image ... failed" and starts with an empty REU (`src/util.c:373`, `reu.c:694`).
6. Keep a hardware log per run: product, firmware and core version (`GET /v1/info`), result, captured frame.
7. Do not interrupt another user's running program or flash on a shared device; power operations need explicit user authorisation.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/gamedev/toolchain.md#7. MODERN packaging: `.cfg` and REU image -->
Rules for a game `.cfg`:
- Write only values from this table. `CPU Speed=48` is valid on both products; `64` is an error on MK1. A second `Turbo Control` line with a label the firmware lacks (for example `C64U Turbo Registers`) is an error: the sidecar path skips it and keeps the valid line, `LOAD_CONFIG` applies nothing.
- The same index means different speeds: index 4 is 5 MHz on MK1 and 6 MHz on Elite II. Choose by label in the `.cfg`; read the speed at run time (`c64://gamedev/techniques` section 10).
- Keep the 1 MHz path: the `.cfg` is not applied on the paths marked "no" above, and a game started that way runs with the user's settings.
- REU image: when `REU Preload` is `Enabled` at firmware start, the firmware loads `REU Preload Image` (default `/Usb0/preload.reu`) once, when that volume is mounted, at `REU Preload Offset`, up to the REU size (`io/c64/reu_preloader.cc:14-115`). A game that must not depend on that loads the file itself: UCI commands and recipes in `c64://ultimate/reu`. Build the image from level files:
```python
import struct, zlib
blocks = [open(f, "rb").read() for f in ("level1.bin", "level2.bin")]  # each at most 64 KB
img = bytearray(256)                     # header: magic, version, count, table (20 rows fit)
img[0:6] = b"GREU\x01" + bytes([len(blocks)])
for i, b in enumerate(blocks):           # row: offset, crc32, length (little endian)
    img[8 + 12*i : 20 + 12*i] = struct.pack("<III", len(img), zlib.crc32(b), len(b))
    img += b + bytes(-len(b) % 256)      # next block on a page boundary
open("preload.reu", "wb").write(img)
```
- Emit the same offsets as an include file for the game (`reu_layout`); the game checks magic and CRCs after loading.

## PETSCII vs Screen Codes

**PETSCII codes** ($00-$FF): Used in BASIC strings, CHR$(), keyboard input, PRINT statements
**Screen codes** ($00-$FF): Values directly written to screen memory ($0400-$07E7)

Conversion: Screen code ≠ PETSCII code. Use charset reference (c64://graphics/character-set) for mapping.

**Usage**:

- BASIC/printing: Use PETSCII codes with CHR$() or PRINT
- Direct screen memory: Use screen codes with POKE to $0400+offset
- Tools: `c64_graphics` with `op: "render_petscii_art"` returns both `petsciiCodes` array and screen memory data

records.name: data/graphics/vic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/graphics/vic-spec.md#Key VIC-II Signals -->
## Key VIC-II Signals

- `A0..A13`: 14-bit multiplexed video address bus (CIA2 bank bits extend reach to 64 KB).
- `D0..D11`: 12-bit data bus; lower 8 bits share CPU bus, upper 4 hit colour RAM.
- `IRQ`: Output to 6510 IRQ pin.
- `BA`: Bus Available; low three cycles before VIC steals phase-2 slots.
- `AEC`: Mirrors CPU AEC; low means VIC drives the bus.
- `LP`: Light-pen input (wired into keyboard matrix).
- `phi_in` / `phi0`: Pixel clock input (8.18 MHz NTSC, 7.88 MHz PAL) and derived 1 MHz system clock output.

records.name: data/graphics/vic-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/graphics/vic-spec.md#Sprites -->
## Sprites

- Data layout: 63 bytes (21 rows x 3 bytes), pointer table = last 8 bytes of video matrix ($03f8-$03ff in bank).
- Each sprite has counters `MC` (6-bit) and `MCBASE`, plus a Y expansion flip-flop.
- DMA enable: in cycles 55-56 the VIC tests `MxE` and `Y == RASTER`; if true, DMA turns on, `MCBASE <- 0`, Y expansion flip-flop cleared when `MxYE` set.
- Cycle 58: `MC <- MCBASE`; sprite becomes visible if DMA on and Y matches raster.
- Sprite fetches: after pointer (`p`) cycle, three `s` cycles read data bytes into a 24-bit shift register; `MC` increments each `s`.
- Display: shift register outputs bits once X matches register; multicolour groups two bits; X expansion halves shift rate; toggling `MxYE` repeats lines for Y expansion.
- Reuse: change Y mid-frame after DMA completes to display same sprite later; horizontal reuse impossible after 24 pixels (shift register empty).
- Priority: sprites ordered 0 highest to 7 lowest; `MxDP=0` places sprite in front of foreground graphics, `1` behind; overall order background < foreground < sprite (subject to `MxDP`) < border.
- Collisions: $d01e (sprite-sprite) and $d01f (sprite-graphics) latch bits until read; only first collision while register clear raises IRQ if enabled.

<!-- Source: data/io/io-spec.md#1. I/O Topology (What connects where) -->
## 1. I/O Topology (What connects where)

- **CIA1 (@ $DC00)** → Keyboard matrix, Joystick Port 1, Joystick Port 2 (via matrix), Paddles select, Lightpen flag, Datasette read IRQ flag, IRQ output.  
- **CIA2 (@ $DD00)** → Serial IEC bus (ATN/CLOCK/DATA), User Port (PB0–PB7; RS‑232 lines), VIC bank select (PRA[1:0]), NMI output.  
- **6510 CPU Port ($0000/$0001)** → Memory map control; **Datasette motor, sense, write** lines. Datasette **read** goes to **CIA1 FLAG**.  
- **Expansion Port** → Direct 6510 bus (A/D/R/W/Φ2/IRQ/NMI/RESET); cartridges/REUs map registers/ROM, **bypassing CIAs**.  
- **SID** → Paddles (analog) POTX/POTY; audio; not covered here.
- **VIC-II** → Lightpen latch; video; not covered here.

(For CIA registers and bit meanings, see `cia-spec.md`.)

records.name: data/io/io-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/io/io-spec.md#3. Serial IEC Bus (Disk, Printers) -->
## 3. Serial IEC Bus (Disk, Printers)

**Physical lines (on CIA2 PRA):**  

- **b3 ATN OUT**, **b4 CLOCK OUT**, **b5 DATA OUT** (active‑low drivers via 7406), **b6 CLOCK IN**, **b7 DATA IN**. Use open‑collector semantics (0V=true/active). Bytes shift **LSB first**, valid on **CLK rising**.

**Protocol sketch:**  

1) Master asserts **ATN**, sends device **TALK/LISTEN** + (optional) **secondary address**.  
2) Data phase with **ATN released**; talker drives DATA, listeners ack. **EOI** marks last byte.  
3) Master sends **UNLISTEN/UNTALK** to end.

> Use KERNAL calls where possible; custom fastloaders may bit‑bang CIA2 lines for speed.

---

records.name: data/io/io-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/io/io-spec.md#5. Keyboard (Matrix Scan) — Detailed -->
## 5. Keyboard (Matrix Scan) — Detailed

**Hardware:** 8×8 matrix via **CIA1**: write **PRA ($DC00)** to select **column**, read **PRB ($DC01)** to sense **rows** (active‑low). Configure **DDRA=$FF**, **DDRB=$00**. Typical scan masks: `$FE,$FD,$FB,$F7,$EF,$DF,$BF,$7F`.
**Algorithm (debounce omitted):**  

```text
init:  DDRA=$FF, DDRB=$00
for col in 0..7:
  PRA = ~(1<<col)            ; one column low, others high
  rows = ~PRB & $7F/$FF      ; read active rows (0=pressed)
  record (col, rows)         ; map to keys
```

**Notes:**  

- Joystick **Port 1** shares PRB bits; pressed directions can alias key bits: e.g. Right = “2” key. Prefer **Port 2** for games.
- **Shift/Ctrl/Commodore** are matrix keys; handle modifiers in lookup.  
- KERNAL scan routine entry in ROM; custom code may be faster/leaner.

<!-- Source: data/printer/printer-commodore-bitmap.md#Minimal pattern example -->
## Minimal pattern example

```basic
10 OPEN1,4
20 A$="":FOR I=1 TO 16:READ B:A$=A$+CHR$(B):NEXT
30 PRINT#1,CHR$(8);A$;A$;A$; : REM 48 COLUMNS IN ONE ROW
40 PRINT#1,CHR$(15); : PRINT#1,CHR$(12):CLOSE1
50 DATA 136,148,162,193,162,148,136,136,156,186,255,186,156,136,235,136
```

**Tips**

- Pre-add **128** to each data byte (bit7=1) before sending.
- For vertical tiling, reprint the same columns with one CR between rows (in bit image mode a line advances 7 dots).
- Keep a row within 480 columns. An MPS-801 prints the line as soon as more than 480 dots are used (MPS-801 manual, section 6 Automatic Printing). The Ultimate printer emulation does not wrap a bit image row: each column advances the head 4 pixels, dots past pixel 1920 are discarded, and no line feed is inserted, so a row longer than 480 columns is cut off at the right edge (1541ultimate@700c7f2fa:software/io/printer/mps_printer.cc:945, mps_printer_cbm.cc:133, mps_printer.h:50).

**Cross‑ref:** Basic text controls in `printer-commodore.md`; overview in `printer-spec.md`.

records.name: data/sound/sid-file-structure.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: data/sound/sid-file-structure.md#Header layout (common fields) -->
## Header layout (common fields)

Offsets are from the start of the file. All multi-byte fields are big-endian.

- +00 — magic (4 bytes): ASCII `PSID` or `RSID`
  - `PSID`: C64-compatible files (player-friendly subset); `RSID`: more strict C64 requirements (no BASIC SYS stubs, tighter hardware expectations)
- +04 — version (uint16): 1..4 (version 5 is also defined by the current HVSC specification)
  - Higher versions extend the header with more fields (see below)
- +06 — dataOffset (uint16): byte offset where the code/data block begins
  - Typically static per version; points to the start of the machine code region
- +08 — loadAddress (uint16): target RAM address for the data block
  - If 0, the first two bytes of the data block contain the load address
- +0A — initAddress (uint16): address to call once at start
  - Accumulator holds the sub-song number minus one when calling init ($00 = song 1)
  - If 0, use `loadAddress` as the init routine address
- +0C — playAddress (uint16): address to call repeatedly to advance playback
  - Usually invoked by the IRQ handler at 50/60 Hz
  - If 0, the code is expected to install its own ISR during init
- +0E — songs (uint16): number of available sub-songs (>= 1)
- +10 — startSong (uint16): default sub-song to start with (1-based)
- +12 — speed (uint32): per-song timing bits (bit i = song i)
  - Bit = 0: use vertical blank (VIC raster; PAL/NTSC rate)
  - Bit = 1: use CIA1 timer-driven playback (~60 Hz)

For version 1, the header ends here and the data begins at offset `$0076` (118); for version 2 and later it begins at `$007C` (124). All `+` offsets in this document are hexadecimal.

# Ultimate turbo benchmark (CPU budget, badlines, sprites, I/O, REU DMA)

**Summary:** Three c64bridge-assembler programs measure CPU cycles per frame, badline and sprite cost, I/O speed and REU DMA rate at every turbo index. Results (2026-11-13, Ultimate 64 Elite fw 3.15a and C64U fw 1.2.1) are in `results/summary.md`; game budgets derived from them are in c64://gamedev/architecture.
**Read when:** you need a measured figure's source, want to rerun or extend the benchmark, or must decode a result block. For game budgets read architecture, not this file.

Measures how many CPU cycles a game really gets per frame on an Ultimate 64 or C64 Ultimate at each turbo setting, and how
fast REU DMA runs. The programs are written for the c64bridge assembler (`c64_program` op `upload_run_asm`): one call, no
toolchain. Measured results are in `results/` (`summary.md`, one JSON file per device and date). The knowledge resources
c64://ultimate/hardware, c64://ultimate/reu, c64://ultimate/upic and c64://gamedev/architecture quote them.

Raw per-point JSON results are in the GitHub repository under data/ultimate/bench/results/; the npm package ships only results/summary.md.

Files: `turbo-cpu.asm`, `turbo-reu.asm`, `turbo-window.asm` (this directory), host script `scripts/turbo-bench.mjs`
(`npm run bench:turbo`).

## Parameters (top of each `.asm`; change the `.equ` values, then upload the whole file)

`turbo-cpu.asm` / `turbo-reu.asm`: `IDX_MASK_LO`, `IDX_MASK_HI` (bit n = speed index n), `COND_MASK`, `VAR_MASK`
(cpu only), `NREP` (1-3), `USE_D031` (1: program writes `$D031`; 0: leave the speed alone, for Manual and TurboEnable
modes), `BADBIT` (`$00` or `$80`, ORed into the `$D031` value), `D030_WRITE`/`D030_VALUE` (write `$D030` once, for the
TurboEnable-bit mode), `SPEED_TABLE` (1 = Ultimate 64 table up to 48 MHz, 2 = C64U/U64E2 table up to 64 MHz),
`NOMINAL_M` (speed in MHz assumed when `USE_D031 = 0`; it only scales the run length and the cycle conversion).
`turbo-window.asm`: `TARGET_IDX`, `BADBIT`, `MAX_ATTEMPTS`.

Speed index to MHz (from `software/u64/u64_config.cc`): Ultimate 64 (Elite): 1 2 3 4 5 6 8 10 12 14 16 20 24 32 40 48.
C64U / Ultimate 64 Elite II: 1 2 3 4 6 8 10 12 14 16 20 24 32 40 48 64. Turbo Control values in the firmware: Off,
Manual, "U64 Turbo Registers", "TurboEnable Bit" (`software/u64/u64_config.cc:328,390`; the same four values were read
from the Ultimate 64 Elite 3.15a and used on the C64 Ultimate 1.2.1). `$D031` bit 7 = 1 suppresses badline and sprite
stalls, 0 keeps stock timing (measured on Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20; c64://ultimate/hardware).

1. `c64_select_backend {"op":"select","backend":"c64u"}` (the configured host decides which Ultimate it is; `"vice"` for
   VICE). Read `c64://platform/status` to confirm.
2. Hardware only. Remember the original settings:
   `c64_config {"op":"get","category":"U64 Specific Settings"}` (all items of the category; save the reply). Note the allowed
   values with `{"op":"get","category":"U64 Specific Settings","item":"Turbo Control"}`, and the same for `"CPU Speed"` and
   `"Badline Timing"`. For the REU program check `{"op":"get","category":"C64 and Cartridge Settings","item":"RAM Expansion Unit"}`
   is `Enabled` (also save its category).
3. Hardware only. Set what the experiment needs, for the registers mode:
   `c64_config {"op":"set","category":"U64 Specific Settings","item":"Turbo Control","value":"<registers value>"}`
   (`U64 Turbo Registers` on the devices measured here). VICE has no turbo: use `USE_D031 = 0`, `NOMINAL_M = 1`,
   `IDX_MASK_LO = 1`, `IDX_MASK_HI = 0`; for the REU program enable the REU first with
   `c64_vice {"op":"resource_set","name":"REU","value":1}` and `{"op":"resource_set","name":"REUsize","value":16384}`.
4. Edit the parameter block of the chosen `.asm`, then
   `c64_program {"op":"upload_run_asm","program":"<full source text>"}` (leave `verify` unset: verification reads the screen).
   The program takes over the machine and does not return to BASIC.
5. Wait the computed time (below) with the client's own wait (shell `sleep`), with no C64 call in between. Seconds:
   cpu `0.56 x nIdx x nCond x nVar x nRep + nIdx x (0.2 + 0.07 x nCond) + 4`;
   reu `nIdx x (0.3 x nCond x nRep + 0.3) + 4`; window `0.12 x MAX_ATTEMPTS + 3`. Add 10 percent. Add about 20 s for every
   speed index that never takes effect (150 attempts x 0.12 s).

## Host script (humans)

```
npm run build                      # the script imports dist/tools/translation/assembler.js (or run it with tsx/bun)
node scripts/turbo-bench.mjs --host <ip> --probe --out out/dev          # prints Turbo Control, CPU Speed, Badline Timing
node scripts/turbo-bench.mjs --host <ip> --suite quick --out out/dev    # about 1.5 min
node scripts/turbo-bench.mjs --host <ip> --suite full  --out out/dev    # about 15 min
node scripts/turbo-bench.mjs --collect out/dev --device "Ultimate 64" --date YYYY-MM-DD \
     --results-out data/ultimate/bench/results/ultimate-64-YYYY-MM-DD.json > summary-part.md
node scripts/turbo-bench.mjs --decode out/dev/cpu-regs-all.bin          # decode one raw result block
```

The script reads the category before it changes anything, sets Turbo Control (and enables the REU if it is off), runs the
programs, restores every changed item in a `finally` block and compares the categories before and after (`RESTORE VERIFIED`
or `RESTORE DIFF`). It never writes flash, resets power or reboots. It reads C64 memory once per run, after the computed time.
On a shared device run one invocation for the whole sequence and do not let another user's program or flash overlap. Set `C64U_PASSWORD` when network protection is enabled. Options:
`--set NAME=VALUE` (parameter override), `--cfg Item=Value`, `--program cpu|reu|window`, `--assemble-only`, `--no-restore`.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/hardware.md#Turbo (CPU speed) -->
Timing (measured U64 and C64U 2026-11-13, PAL; rerun: c64://ultimate/hardware#rerun):
- The CPU gets one sub-slot per phi2 less than the nominal factor at the two top entries: 47 cycles per phi2 at 48 MHz (2,961 per line), 63 at 64 MHz (3,969 per line). Up to 32 MHz the count equals the nominal factor. The VIC-II keeps priority, and CIA timers, raster and SID run in C64 time.
- Cycles per PAL frame at 48 / 64 MHz: screen blanked 923,875 / 1,238,387; screen on 873,784 / 1,170,907; screen on plus 8 double-height sprites 836,375 / 1,121,520. At 1 MHz: 19,656 / 18,575 / 17,783. Badlines cost 5.5 % at every speed and 8 sprites a further 4.1 %. With `$D031` bit 7 set the screen-on loss is below 0.2 %. In `U64 Turbo Registers` mode the `Badline Timing` item did not change the loop counts.
- I/O reads are slower than RAM at high speed: a `lda $D012` loop ran at 42 of 47 cycles per phi2 at 48 MHz and 56.5 of 63 at 64 MHz. `sta $D020` runs at RAM speed. A CIA read loop reached 8.8 cycles per phi2 at most (7.5 at 8-12 MHz). `sta abs,x` to I/O adds a dummy read.
- Accesses to the cartridge port and to real SID chips in the sockets run at 1 MHz; UltiSID writes stay inside the FPGA.
- IEC bit-banging and cycle-counted 1 MHz raster code fail under turbo. KERNAL `LOAD` from a 1541 (IEC) worked at 16 and 48 MHz (measured U64).
- After `run_prg` the core keeps 1 MHz for 2.55 s (U64) and 2.57 s (C64U) after program start, whatever `$D031` holds (measured 2026-11-13). Wait until two consecutive timing loops agree before timing-critical code.

## Data streams (U64 family and C64U; not U2 family)

UDP streams to a host. Store `Data Streams`: `Stream VIC to` (default `239.0.1.64:11000`), `Stream Audio to` (`239.0.1.65:11001`), `Stream Debug to` (`239.0.1.66:11002`), `Debug Stream Mode` (`6510 Only`, `VIC Only`, `6510 & VIC`, `1541 Only`, `6510 & 1541`, `6510 w/IEC`, `6510 & VIC w/IEC`).
- REST `PUT /v1/streams/{video|audio|debug}:start?ip=<addr[:port]>` and `:stop` (`software/api/route_streams.cc:20-115`). Without a port: 11000 video, 11001 audio, 11002 debug. `ip` is an address, a host name or a multicast group 232.0.0.0-239.255.255.255. Errors: 404 for an unknown stream name or an unresolvable host, 500 when the wired Ethernet link is down or has no IP. `:stop` on a stopped stream returns 200.
- The streams leave through the wired Ethernet port even when WiFi carried the request. Video and debug share hardware: starting video stops debug.
- `palette=1` (video only; otherwise 400): the device also sends 60-byte palette packets, twice per second: video header with line 239, 384 pixels, 1 line, 4 bpp, encoding 1, 16 RGB triples from byte 12, bytes 0-1 a counter. The setting is device-wide; the most recent `start` sets it. A video parser skips or decodes packets with encoding 1.
- Video header (12 bytes, little-endian): sequence u16, frame u16, line u16 (bit 15 = last packet of the frame), pixels per line u16, lines per packet u8, bits per pixel u8, encoding u16. Measured U64: 384x272 pixels, 4 bpp, 68 packets of 4 lines (780 bytes), 50 frames per second, encoding 0.
- Audio packet: 2-byte sequence, then 192 stereo frames of signed 16-bit samples, 47,982.89 Hz on PAL (measured U64).
- After each video or audio start the device sends one 2-byte datagram `00 00` from another source port (measured U64); a receiver ignores datagrams shorter than a header.
- The U2 family builds do not contain these routes (`target/u64*/.../Makefile` list `route_streams.cc`; the U2 makefiles do not), so they answer 404.

- `X-Password` header: when `Network Password` (store `Network Settings`) is not empty, every REST request needs it; a wrong or missing header gives 403 `Forbidden.`.
- U64 family only: `PUT machine:poweroff` and `machine:input` (U2 family: 501, `software/api/route_machine.cc:186-216`, `route_input.cc:718-747`); `machine:debugreg` (read/write the FPGA debug register `$D7FF`) and the `streams` routes (U2 family: route absent, 404). All products: `machine:reset|reboot|pause|resume|menu_button|menu_screen|readmem|writemem|measure|heap`, `runners:*`, `drives`, `configs`, `files/{path}:info|create_d64|create_d71|create_d81|create_dnp`, `GET /v1/help?command=`, `GET /v1/version` (returns `0.1`), `GET /v1/info`.
- `GET machine:readmem`: `length` 1-65536, default 256; length 0 or 65537 gives 400 `Invalid length`; a range past `$FFFF` gives 400 `Memory read exceeds location $FFFF` (measured U64). The read is a DMA read in the current bank configuration: `$A000` and `$E000` return ROM when ROM is banked in, and a read of `$DD0D` clears the CIA2 interrupt flags as a CPU read does (measured U64).
- `PUT machine:writemem?address=<hex>&data=<hex>`: 1-128 bytes; 129 bytes give 400 `Maximum length of 128 bytes exceeded...` and write nothing. `POST machine:writemem?address=<hex>` with the bytes as body: a start plus length past `$FFFF` gives 400, but a 65,537-byte body at `$0000` returned 200 `0000-FFFF` and dropped the last byte (measured U64). Writes go through the current bank configuration, so `$D020` reaches the VIC while I/O is mapped.

<!-- Source: data/ultimate/multisid.md#Run-time control from the C64 -->
## Run-time control from the C64

- UCI is off by default: `C64 and Cartridge Settings / Command Interface=Enabled` is required; read `$DF1D` for `$C9`. Registers `$DF1C-$DF1F` (see c64://ultimate/uci). The game cannot enable UCI itself.
- `LOAD_CONFIG` (target 4, command `$50`, message `04 50 <path>`) applies a `.cfg` and effectuates the changed stores at once while the program runs, when every line is valid (status `00,OK`). Any invalid line gives `89` and applies no store (c64://ultimate/uci). Device: works with `/Temp/name.cfg` (put there by FTP; a game writes it via the DOS target). The reply data is the parse log; a store the device lacks gives `Line N: Store name '...' not found; section ignored.` and status `00,OK`.
- Labels equal the REST names; example: Recipe above.
- The 6510 cannot write the decoder settings directly, and no UCI command reads a setting. A `.cfg` with the same name as a PRG, CRT, TAP, D64 or G64 file is applied when that file is started from the file browser (`software/filetypes/filetype_{prg,crt,tap,d64,g64}.cc`).
- Restore: make a restore `.cfg` at install time from the host (`GET /v1/configs/<store>` for `SID Addressing`, `Audio Mixer`, ...) and `LOAD_CONFIG` it on exit after silencing the chips (device: restores exactly the listed items).
- Flash: changes live in RAM; they are saved only by `configs:save_to_flash` or the menu's save prompt, so a later menu visit can persist the game's map (source).
- Host: `PUT /v1/configs/<store>/<item>?value=...` (RAM only) or `c64_config`.

<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Getting data into the REU -->
## Getting data into the REU

| Path | Works from host? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| UCI DOS LOAD_REU (`01 21`, open file first) | by a running program | recommended for shipped games; file to REU without the C64; one command moves up to 16 MB minus the start; see c64://ultimate/uci |
| Menu: file browser, `.reu` file, load into REU | no (menu) | whole file to offset 0 |
| `REU Preload` (config) | partly | **boot only** (see below) |
| Stash stub + `machine:writemem` | yes | slow but scriptable |
| `runners:modplay` (PUT file / POST body) | yes | loads a MOD into REU offset 0 and plays it; overwrites the REU; needs the sampler |
| UCI control LOAD_REU `04 08 <3+ filler bytes>` | by a running program | loads the file named in `REU Preload Image` at `REU Preload Offset` (needs `RAM Expansion Unit` Enabled; `REU Preload` can be Disabled): the run-time way to repeat the preload; reply 4-byte LE count + text; `04 09` saves the REU back to that file (old file kept as `.bu`); see c64://ultimate/uci |

- There is no REST endpoint that writes REU memory. `machine:writemem`/`readmem` cover only C64 `$0000-$FFFF` (DMA on the cartridge bus, CPU stalls briefly).
- **Preload runs once at firmware boot** (`software/io/c64/reu_preloader.cc:14-80`). It is armed only if `REU Preload` is `Enabled` when the firmware starts; it waits for the volume of `REU Preload Image` to appear, then 25 ticks of the 200 Hz RTOS clock (125 ms), loads `min(file size, REU Size - offset)` bytes and ends its task. `machine:reset`, C64 reboot and `run_prg` do not reload it; setting it by REST after boot does not arm it; a power cycle or menu reboot does. To repeat it without reboot use UCI Control `04 08`. The image need not equal the REU size (VICE `-reuimage` does require exactly that size).
- **Stash stub pattern:** a small resident PRG with a mailbox (REU address, C64 address, length, command, trigger byte written last). The host writes a 16 KB chunk to C64 RAM with `machine:writemem`, fills the mailbox, trigger last; the stub stashes it and clears the trigger; the host polls the trigger, then verifies by fetching back. Hash chunks to skip unchanged ones (the REU survives resets).
- `.reu` files are raw REU dumps without header. The menu action "Save REU Memory" writes `REU Size` bytes (`software/io/c64/c64_subsys.cc:296-315`). DOS LOAD_REU/SAVE_REU address a 16 MB REU.
- Image layout: header (magic, version, block table of id/flags/24-bit offset/length), per-block checksums checked at boot.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/reu.md#Patterns for games -->
## Patterns for games

- **Level/map streaming:** keep tile maps in the REU page-aligned; once per frame, after the raster IRQ passed the visible area, fetch one 256-byte column or row into an off-screen buffer. Measured on a C64U at 64 MHz: one 256-byte fetch per frame for 500 frames, no glitches.
- **Charset/sprite swap into a VIC bank** between frames: fetch the new 2 KB charset or sprite blocks into the inactive part of the VIC bank, then flip `$D018`/`$DD00` in the next IRQ. Fetching 2,048 bytes takes 2.07 ms at 1 MHz (0.99 B/us), 0.57 ms at 48 MHz and 0.48 ms at 64 MHz (measured fetch rates above).
- **Bitmap/screen swap:** 8000 + 1000 + 1000 bytes take 10.1 ms at 1 MHz (half a PAL frame), 2.8 ms at 48 MHz, 2.3 ms at 64 MHz: start after the bottom IRQ, flip in the next top IRQ, or hide it under a fade. Colour RAM needs I/O mapped in.
- **Digi samples (design pattern):** 4-bit samples in the REU, a 256-byte ring in RAM, a CIA timer IRQ that writes one sample to `$D418` per tick (8000 Hz = CIA timer value 122 on PAL, 985,248 Hz / 8000 - 1), and a 64-byte fetch each time 64 samples were consumed. Let the IRQ own the REU or wrap access in `sei`. `$D418` bits 4-7 are filter/voice-3 bits: write the whole value. Alternative: the Ultimate Audio sampler (`$DF20-$DFFF`, `Map Ultimate Audio $DF20-DFFF`) plays from REU without the CPU; register map and REU addressing in c64://ultimate/hardware (Ultimate Audio sampler).
- A raster IRQ and the main loop must not both program the REU: one owner, or `sei`/`cli` around main-loop use. Overlays: architecture section 5C.

## Target 3: Network (client only, reads never block)

| Cmd | Name | Args | Reply |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | IDENTIFY | - | `ULTIMATE-II NETWORK INTERFACE V1.0` |
| 02 | GET_INTERFACE_COUNT | - | count |
| 03 | SET_INTERFACE | `<if>` | select interface |
| 04-06 | GET_NETADDR / GET_IPADDR / SET_IPADDR | `<if> [12 bytes]` | MAC (6); IP, mask, gateway (4 each) |
| 07 | OPEN_TCP | `<port:16> <host or IP>` | socket handle |
| 08 | OPEN_UDP | `<port:16> <host or IP>` | handle (connected socket) |
| 09 | CLOSE_SOCKET | `<h>` | status |
| 10 | READ_SOCKET | `<h> <len:16>` | `<count:16>` then payload |
| 11 | WRITE_SOCKET | `<h> <data>` | 2-byte count sent |

- OPEN_TCP and OPEN_UDP resolve host names themselves. Interfaces are numbered from 0; query each with GET_IPADDR and use one whose IP is not `0.0.0.0`.
- READ_SOCKET answers at once; with nothing waiting the status is `02,NO DATA: <errno>`. Poll once per frame or less often. The source (since 2026-08-27) accepts up to 1472 bytes per read and returns them in several reply blocks; a longer request gives `82`; a UDP datagram longer than the request gives `04,DATAGRAM TRUNCATED: <n>` (`network_target.h:41`, `network_target.cc:540-556`). Request at most 512 bytes so that older firmware answers in one block.
- After `01,CONNECTION CLOSED BY HOST` the handle is already released.
- OPEN_TCP blocks until the connection is made or fails; open sockets before the game loop, behind a status screen. Never connect to the device's own address. Timing of the call, measured with the jiffy clock (measured on Ultimate 64 Elite, firmware 3.15a, 2026-11-20): `03 07 50 00 "192.0.2.1"` (TEST-NET-1, no host answers) returned `11,ERROR ON CONNECT: 113` after 18.02 to 18.35 s (3 runs: 1081, 1089 and 1101 jiffies, 1 jiffy = 1/60 s). `03 07 50 00 "h6-nohost.invalid"` returned `84,UNRESOLVED HOST` in 0 or 1 jiffy (17 ms or less).
- 16 sockets (`NET_MAX_SOCKETS`), all closed at a C64 reset. The public firmware has no inbound listener: multiplayer needs a relay server or UDP.
- Wire: `03 07 <portlo> <porthi> <host>`; `03 10 <h> 00 02` reads 512.

| 03 | FINISH_CAPTURE | - | ends a tape capture (not for games) |
| 08 / 09 | LOAD_REU / SAVE_REU | `<3+ filler bytes>` | no filename is read: `08` loads the file set in `REU Preload Image` into the REU at `REU Preload Offset` (up to `REU Size` minus offset; needs `RAM Expansion Unit` Enabled, `REU Preload` may be Disabled); `09` writes the REU back to that file (an existing file is renamed `.bu`). Reply: 4-byte little-endian result (bytes moved; -1 file error, -2 REU disabled, -3 offset past `REU Size`) plus the upper-case log text; statuses `81` (command shorter than 5 bytes), `84`, `85`, `86` (`control_target.cc:345-378`, `software/io/c64/reu_preloader.cc:82-176`). DOS `21`/`22` take any file and offset |
| 0F | U64_SAVEMEM | `[<filename>]` | U64 family; saves the 64 KB RAM to the file (default `/temp/c64_memory.bin`) with the C64 halted; status `00,OK` or `87,DISK ERR: <text>` |
| 28 | GET_HWINFO | `[sub]` | 0 (or omitted) = product string; 1 = SID decoder list (count, 5 bytes each; c64://ultimate/multisid); other: `81` |
| 11 / 12 | DECODE_TRACK / ENCODE_TRACK | | disk track tools (not for games) |
| 20 | EASYFLASH | | EasyFlash sector tool (not for games) |
| 29 | GET_DRVINFO | `[mode]` | count, then 3 bytes per drive: type (`00` 1541, `01` 1571, `02` 1581, `0F` SoftwareIEC, `50` printer), IEC address (mode 1 or omitted: effective address; 0: configured address), power `00`/`01` (`control_target.cc:216-248`) |
| 30-35 | drive A/B power | - | `30` A on, `31` A off, `32` B on, `33` B off, `34`/`35` read power (`off`/`on `) |

## Target 5: SoftwareIEC (fast load into C64 RAM)

| Cmd | Name | Args | Reply / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | IDENTIFY | - | `SOFTWARE IEC TARGET V1.0` |
| 10 | LOAD_SU | `<sec> <verify> <addr:16> 00 00 <name>` | 2 bytes: file load address; if sec = 0, `addr` is used |
| 11 | LOAD_EX | `<sec> <verify>` | copies into RAM; status `00` + end address:16 |
| 12 | SAVE | `<verify> <sec> <start:16> <end:16> <name>` | PRG file |
| 13 | OPEN | `<sec> <unused> <name>` | opens a channel of the SoftwareIEC drive; status `00,OK` |
| 14 | CLOSE | `<sec> <unused>` | status `00,OK` |
| 15 | CHKIN | `<sec> <unused>` | reply = bytes read from the channel; status `$00`, or `$03` without input channel. Measured U64: CHKIN 15 returned `73,U64HD ULTIMATE DOS V2.0,00,00`; the bytes arrive over several exchanges |
| 16 | CHKOUT | `<sec> <unused> <data>` | sends `<data>` to the channel; with `sec` = `$Fx` the data is a file name to open, with `$Ex` the channel is closed (`softiec_target.cc:305-333`); status `00,OK` |
| 20-23 | ADD_PARTITION / DEL_PARTITION / GET_FATNAME / GET_IECNAME | | partition and name mapping (not for games) |

Binary status (`softiec_target.cc:12-21,185`): `00` OK, `01` not found, `02` save error, `03` no input channel, `04` unknown command, `05` IEC drive not available, `06` invalid params, `07` invalid name, `08` invalid partition, `09` invalid dir, `80` verify error. The firmware stops the C64 during the copy, writes into the flat RAM view (RAM under I/O and ROM), and stops at 64 KB.
- `IEC Drive` (store `SoftIEC Drive Settings`, since 2026-09-23): `UCI Only` (default), `Enabled` or `Disabled` (`iec_drive.cc:31,37,165`); `Disabled` makes every command of this target answer `05`. Fall back to DOS OPEN/READ/CLOSE.

records.text:
<!-- Source: data/ultimate/upic.md#Game architecture on Upic -->
1. **Display IRQ plus main loop.** The raster IRQ draws the picture; the main loop runs in the remaining time. A commit hook at the end of the IRQ (after the picture) applies everything the main loop prepared (scroll offsets), so nothing tears. Main loop writes only rows/columns that are currently hidden.
2. **Frame schedule with cycle allowances.** Example budget out of 268,300 free cycles (240 rows): scroll and exposed terrain 60k, objects 30k, one palette update 3k, one UCI state-machine step 2k, simulation 15k, background work up to 40k. Defer any step that does not fit to the next frame; never delay the picture.
3. **Ring-buffer scrolling.** Vertical: each column is exactly 256 bytes, so starting the renderer's row index at `row0` scrolls by wrapping for free; only the newly exposed row (192 stores) is written. Horizontal: re-point the renderer's column operands (high bytes only, since columns are page-aligned): one new column is one 256-byte REU fetch. Granularity: 2 pixels per step horizontally, 1 row vertically. Keep a margin (for example 8 hidden rows and 2 hidden byte columns) where new content is written. Patching generated renderer code is tied to the library version.
4. **Software sprites.** 8x8 tile = 4 byte columns x 8 rows = 32 bytes, stored column-major so a byte column copies straight into a picture column. Shapes: data plus mask (a nybble of `$F` = transparent), save-under buffers, a cap on shapes per frame. Horizontal positions move in whole byte columns (2 pixels); an odd x needs a second copy of the shape shifted by one nybble.

## Purpose

This document is a concise implementation reference for C64 Bridge maintainers and LLM agents that need to understand how the VICE backend maps to the VICE binary monitor protocol.

For normal MCP use, agents should call the existing C64 Bridge tools instead of constructing VICE packets directly.

Recommended C64 Bridge entry points:

| Need | C64 Bridge tool | Typical operation |
|---|---|---|
| Select the VICE backend | `c64_select_backend` | `select` |
| Read or write memory | `c64_memory` | `read`, `write`, `read_screen`, `wait_for_text` |
| Debug registers and checkpoints | `c64_debug` | `get_registers`, `set_registers`, `create_checkpoint`, `list_checkpoints`, `step`, `step_return` |
| Send keyboard or joystick input | `c64_input` | `write_text`, `key`, `joystick` |
| Capture emulator display | `c64_graphics` | `capture_frame` |
| Reset or continue execution | `c64_system`, `c64_debug` | `reset`, `continue_execution` |
| Read or write VICE resources | `c64_vice` | `resource_get`, `resource_set` |

---

## Command Frame

```text
Offset  Size  Field
0       1     STX = 0x02
1       1     API version = 0x02
2       4     Command body length as u32
6       4     Request ID as u32
10      1     Command type as u8
11      N     Command body
````

```text
command_body_length = total_command_packet_length - 11
```

The command length excludes the whole command header.

<!-- Source: data/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md#`0x01` - Memory Get -->
## `0x01` - Memory Get

Reads memory from inclusive range `[SA..EA]`.

```text
cmd: FX:u8 | SA:u16 | EA:u16 | MS:u8 | BI:u16
rsp: 0x01 | ML:u16 | MM:bytes[ML]
```

| Field | Meaning                  |
| ----- | ------------------------ |
| `FX`  | Read causes side effects |
| `SA`  | Start address            |
| `EA`  | End address, inclusive   |
| `MS`  | Memspace                 |
| `BI`  | Bank ID                  |
| `ML`  | Memory length            |
| `MM`  | Memory bytes             |

For `$0000..$ffff`, `ML` may be `0`, meaning 65536 bytes.

C64 Bridge mapping:

| MCP tool     | Operation       |
| ------------ | --------------- |
| `c64_memory` | `read`          |
| `c64_memory` | `read_screen`   |
| `c64_memory` | `wait_for_text` |

---

## Internal VICE Backend Rules

The C64 Bridge VICE backend should:

- keep binary monitor request IDs internal;
- correlate direct replies by request ID;
- treat the protocol as asynchronous;
- buffer or route asynchronous events separately from command responses;
- decode binary data internally;
- return LLM-readable JSON from MCP tools;
- return memory and display payloads as hex strings or files, not raw byte arrays;
- cache register metadata from `REGISTERS_AVAILABLE`;
- cache bank metadata from `BANKS_AVAILABLE`;
- refresh cached metadata if the VICE machine type changes.

<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md#Memory (0x01–0x02) -->
### Memory (0x01–0x02)

#### 0x01 – Memory Get

- Request: `[0] sidefx (0 = peek, 1 = normal read), [1–2] start address, [3–4] end address, [5] memspace, [6–7] bank`
- Response (`0x01`): `[0–1] byte count (uint16), [2+] data block`
- Notes: Addresses are inclusive; the monitor validates memspace and bank (`0x02` or `0x81` on failure). During the transfer `sidefx` temporarily overrides the global `sidefx` flag.

#### 0x02 – Memory Set

- Request: `[0] sidefx (0 = poke, 1 = write with side effects), [1–2] start address, [3–4] end address, [5] memspace, [6–7] bank, [8+] payload`
- Response (`0x02`): empty body
- Notes: Payload length must equal `(end - start + 1)` or the monitor returns `0x80`. Writes loop byte-by-byte through `mon_set_mem_val_ex`, masking the address to 16 bits.

records.name: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md
records.text:
<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-binary-monitor-spec.md#Checkpoints and Conditions (0x11–0x22) -->
### Checkpoints and Conditions (0x11–0x22)

#### 0x11 – Checkpoint Get

- Request: `[0–3] checkpoint number`
- Response (`0x11`): checkpoint info (see §6)
- Notes: Unknown checkpoints return `0x01`.

#### 0x12 – Checkpoint Set

- Request: `[0–1] start address, [2–3] end address, [4] stop flag, [5] enabled flag, [6] memory-op mask, [7] temporary flag`, optional byte `[8]` selects the memspace
- Response (`0x11`): the newly created checkpoint
- Notes: The memory-op mask uses bits `e_load`=1, `e_store`=2, and `e_exec`=4. If the body is at least 9 bytes the optional memspace overrides the default `e_comp_space`. The monitor disables the checkpoint if the enabled flag is zero.

#### 0x13 – Checkpoint Delete

- Request: `[0–3] checkpoint number`
- Response (`0x13`): empty
- Notes: Fails with `0x01` if the checkpoint does not exist.

#### 0x14 – Checkpoint List

- Request: empty body
- Response: one or more `0x11` messages (same request ID) for each checkpoint, followed by a `0x14` containing `[0–3] total checkpoint count`
- Notes: The per-checkpoint responses set `hit = 0`.

#### 0x15 – Checkpoint Toggle

- Request: `[0–3] checkpoint number, [4] enable flag`
- Response (`0x15`): empty
- Notes: Returns `0x01` when the checkpoint is missing.

#### 0x22 – Condition Set

- Request: `[0–3] checkpoint number, [4] expression length, [5+] expression text`
- Response (`0x22`): empty
- Notes: The monitor appends a NUL byte after the provided text and executes `cond <id> if (<expr>)`. Expression syntax matches the CLI monitor. Failure to parse or execute yields `0x8F`.

<!-- Source: doc/vice/vice-bm-vs-c64u-rest.md#Memory and CPU State -->
## Memory and CPU State

| Capability | VICE Binary Monitor | Ultimate REST API | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Memory read | 🟢 `0x01` Memory Get — body `[sidefx,start_lo,start_hi,end_lo,end_hi,memspace,bank_lo,bank_hi]`; response `0x01` with length and data block. | 🟡 `GET /v1/machine:readmem?address=$ADDR&length=$LEN` (DMA map, default length 256). | Binary monitor supports memspaces and banks; REST access is limited to the flattened DMA-visible map and must not wrap past `$FFFF`. |
| Memory write | 🟢 `0x02` Memory Set — request extends Memory Get body with the payload bytes for `[start,end]`. | 🟡 `PUT /v1/machine:writemem?address=$ADDR&data=...` or `POST /v1/machine:writemem` with binary attachment. | Monitor enforces payload length match and offers side-effect control; REST writes up to 128 bytes per call using the current DMA mapping. |
| Register snapshot | 🟢 `0x31` Registers Get — body `[memspace]`; response lists `(size,id,value_lo,value_hi)` tuples. | 🔴 Not available (except `GET /v1/machine:debugreg` for `$D7FF`). | REST lacks general-purpose register visibility; only the Ultimate 64 debug register is exposed. |
| Register update | 🟢 `0x32` Registers Set — `[memspace,count,{size,id,value_lo,value_hi,...}]`; response echoes `0x31`. | 🔴 Not available. | Direct CPU register writes require the monitor. |
| Banks enumeration | 🟢 `0x82` Banks Available — lists bank IDs and names for `e_comp_space`. | 🔴 Not available. | REST cannot query cartridge banks; the monitor is needed for bank-aware tools. |
| Register catalog | 🟢 `0x83` Registers Available — reports register IDs, bit widths, and names. | 🔴 Not available. | REST offers no equivalent metadata. |
| VICE info | 🟡 `0x85` VICE Info — returns `VERSION_RC_NUMBER` and optional revision bytes. | 🟢 `GET /v1/version`, `GET /v1/info`. | REST delivers richer device metadata (product, firmware, FPGA); monitor only returns emulator build numbers. |
| Ping | 🟢 `0x81` Ping — empty request/response. | 🟢 `GET /v1/version` (lightweight health check). | Monitor ping also verifies API negotiation (error `0x82` on bad version). |

| Capability | VICE Binary Monitor | Ultimate REST API | Notes |

| Create checkpoint | 🟢 `0x12` Checkpoint Set — `[start,end,stop,enabled,op_mask,temporary,(optional)memspace]`; response `0x11`. | 🔴 Not available. | Only the monitor exposes code/data breakpoints. |

| Delete checkpoint | 🟢 `0x13` Checkpoint Delete — `[checknum]`. | 🔴 Not available. | — |
| Toggle checkpoint | 🟢 `0x15` Checkpoint Toggle — `[checknum,enable]`. | 🔴 Not available. | — |
| List checkpoints | 🟢 `0x14` Checkpoint List — emits one `0x11` per entry then `0x14` with total count. | 🔴 Not available. | — |
| Conditional breakpoint | 🟢 `0x22` Condition Set — `[checknum,len,expr_bytes]`. | 🔴 Not available. | Expressions mirror CLI monitor syntax. |
| Step/advance | 🟢 `0x71` Advance Instructions — `[step_over,count_lo,count_hi]`. | 🔴 Not available. | REST cannot single-step; use pause/resume only. |
| Execute until return | 🟢 `0x73` Execute Until Return. | 🔴 Not available. | — |

| Jam/stop/resume events | 🟢 Async responses `0x61/0x62/0x63` with request ID `0xffffffff`. | 🔴 Not available. | REST lacks push notifications; clients must poll status. |
